title: VIRTUA TENNIS / SEGA NAOMI UNIVERSAL
variant: Original Virtua Tennis (Sega Professional Tennis, 1999) in the white standing NAOMI Universal shown in Sega Amusements Europe's operator flyer; not the red conversion pedestal or Virtua Tennis 2
preview_note: 40 x 60 px | white NAOMI / green title / 2 sticks + 6 physical actions / flyer display

dimensions.flyer: W 75 cm, D 98 cm, H 180 cm, 29-inch 31 kHz monitor; billboard adds height
dimensions.sprite: Estimated world-space geometry; base/CRT/rails/billboard are separate. Low-resolution proportions are not dimensionally exact.

flyer.purpose: Archived Sega Amusements Europe printed operator flyer. Corroborates NAOMI hardware, original game's eight tennis players, white standing shell, green game marquee, orange lamp, dark rails, white two-station deck and photographed tennis-court display. Supplies rectified marquee, deck and screen.
flyer.rights: Underlying Sega artwork/trademarks and printed flyer copyright remain retained. Archive hosting is not publisher authorization. Scan author, restoration status and redistribution permission are unknown.

naomi_shell.purpose: Generic NAOMI Universal three-quarter photograph and documented cabinet construction: standing rails, projecting control panel, open knee space, lower enclosure and deep rear CRT pod. Geometry corroboration only; this different game's panel and loading screen are NOT extracted.
naomi_shell.rights: Photo author and image-specific license unverified; underlying Sega hardware/artwork rights retained. Wiki access does not establish image redistribution permission.

conversion_cabinet.purpose: Research-only red/yellow/blue operator conversion pedestal showing original Virtua Tennis, not Virtua Tennis 2. Distinct alternative shell; none of its red shell, green bezel or blue deck is mixed into the selected NAOMI variant.
conversion_cabinet.rights: Underlying Sega game artwork/trademarks retained. Photo author, cabinet provenance and redistribution rights unknown; archive hosting is not publisher authorization.

conversion_controls.purpose: Research-only alternative conversion panel: confirms three physical action buttons and separate Start per station, despite two used shot actions. Not used as the white NAOMI panel texture.
conversion_controls.rights: Underlying Sega operator artwork/trademarks retained. Photo author, replacement-print authenticity and redistribution rights unknown; archive hosting is not publisher authorization.

uncertainties: Chosen original-game white NAOMI Universal is supported by Sega Europe's flyer, not claimed to be the only factory or conversion cabinet. Exact region/revision and original-versus-restored archive scan authenticity are unverified.

The title, white panel and actual tennis display are rectified from the flyer cabinet photograph, not publisher-hosted production masters or a local emulator capture. Detail is limited by the printed scan; screen brightness receives 1.15x at sprite scale.

Three raised physical actions per station follow the photographed three-button panels. Virtua Tennis uses Shot/Lob (two actions); Start details remain in the deck photograph, not additional modeled raised buttons. Button colors/spacing and ball-top shape are small-scale approximations of the selected flyer, not the red conversion's hardware.

No dedicated tennis-player side print is evidenced. Sides remain plain dark rails with white edging and a narrow red seam. The generic shell photo's NAOMI lettering and different game's six-button deck/loading display are not reused.

The yellow-looking space under the flyer's control deck is the flyer background visible through the open frame, not invented yellow front artwork. Lower service/cash doors and rear vents are geometry estimates corroborated by the generic shell.
Sega artwork and photograph redistribution rights remain unresolved. Archive/wiki availability is not deployment permission.

Skin vtennis selects the existing vtennisg GD-ROM game entry. The original game's operator flyer guides the cabinet; it is not asserted to be a GD-ROM-specific decal kit. Catalog core, files, player count and lockstep settings are preserved; no map placement or emulator work is part of this art.
